# Unlocking a region's last locked column erases that column

## Context

Promoted from @neo-opus-grace's defect-note of 2026-09-19 15:13Z, reproduced independently before filing: real Chromium (Playwright e2e rig), dev@4802862b73, fixture `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing`, grid `#grid-cell-editing`, remote methods only (`Neo.worker.App.setConfigs({id: <the note column>, locked: null})`).

## The Problem

`note` is that grid's only locked-end column.

| | header buttons | `note` cells | grid bodies |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | Code · # · Name · Score · City · **Note** | 6, in the end body | 3 |
| after `locked: null` | Code · # · Name · Score · City | **0** | 2 |

The column instance lives on (`dataField: 'note'`, `locked: null`), no error is logged, and nothing brings the column back. Unlocking a column whose region keeps another locked column works: the region survives, and the button moves.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/Container.mjs#onColumnLockChange` re-adds the sorted columns; the collection's `mutate` runs `#onColumnsMutate` (`:1185`): `refreshRegionColumns()` → `createOrUpdateSubGrids()` → `headerWrapper.applyColumnButtonOrder(...)`.
- `createOrUpdateSubGrids()` calls `src/grid/header/Wrapper.mjs#updateHeaders` (`:154`), which **destroys** the toolbar of a region that holds no column any more (`:204–207` for the end, `:182–185` for the start). At that moment the column that just left the region still has its header button INSIDE that toolbar, so the button is destroyed with it.
- `#applyColumnButtonOrder` (`:84`) runs afterwards and re-homes buttons through `getButton(dataField)` — which finds nothing for the moved column. With no button, `toolbar.passSizeToBody()` yields no `columnPositions` entry, and the gaining body renders no cell for it.
- The start region has the same teardown and the same order, so its last column is exposed the same way.

## The Fix

In `header.Wrapper#updateHeaders`: create or refresh the toolbars of the regions that hold columns first; when a region emptied at runtime, re-home the buttons (`applyColumnButtonOrder`) while every target toolbar exists; only then destroy the emptied toolbar. The buttons are moved, never rebuilt.

Arms on `#grid-cell-editing-pooled` (one locked-start column `c0`, one locked-end column `c39`), through two new actions of the fixture's `gridDriver.mjs`: after unlocking each, its header button and its cells are in the center region; locking it again brings the region back with the column in it. Red on dev.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unlocking a grid's only locked-end column keeps its header button and its cells, in the center region; the same for the only locked-start column.
- [ ] Locking the column again re-creates the region with the column in it.
- [ ] The header button instance is moved, not rebuilt.
- [ ] The arms are red on dev; grid e2e, component and unit tiers stay green.

## Out of Scope

- An edit open on the moving column while its region empties (the hold path has its own leaves under #18762).
- The grid body teardown order in `createOrUpdateSubGrids` beyond what the header fix needs.
